# Builds and the site's other generated files

- `messages_{ao,ae}.json`: generated **and committed** viewer sidecar holding the game's own message tables, one array per table indexed by the id an object carries (`{"lcd": ["", "The profits justify the means.", …], "hintfly": [...]}`). AO carries both tables; AE has no HintFly.
  - Read **off the discs**, unlike the sidecars derived from the decomp alone, so it is written by a normal build rather than by `--emit-field-data`. The decomp carries both LCD tables in source, but those are the PC build's and differ from PS1's in wording, not only in button names: PSX AO 52 ends "while you run" where PC adds "using [Run]", and PSX AE 73 spells out a two-button combo where PC names a dedicated key.
  - Each table is a pointer array plus a 4-byte-aligned string blob compiled into the **level overlays** (`*.OVL`), not into `SLUS_*`, and duplicated identically into every overlay whose level needs it. `write_messages` extracts every copy and requires them all to agree, so the per-level question is re-answered on each build rather than trusted from one reading.
  - `string_table` anchors on a known string rather than an address, which derives the overlay's load base from the data; it finds the table by the run of gaps between the first strings and believes it only if the slot past its declared end points nowhere, which is what makes the length self-proving.
  - Messages keep the font's button-command code points (0x08-0x13) rather than any name for them: the viewer owns the naming, as it owns the enum transforms. A code outside that set fails the build. The 31-space scroll-in lead every LCD message opens with is stripped at emit.
  - `message_json` writes those codes `\u00XX`, because json's shorthand would put `\n` and `\t` mid-sentence where they read as whitespace; no message contains a backslash, which is what makes the rewrite exact.
- `sprites_{ao,ae}.json` and `cams/{ao,ae}/sprites/<set>/*.png`: generated **and committed** sprite atlases and their animation table, written game-wide by a normal build off the discs: one copy of every animation the Objects-as-themselves toggle can ask for, named as in [tools/data/sprite_anims.json](../tools/data/sprite_anims.json) (`Slig_Idle`, `bg:6016` for a camera-resident background animation, `Mudokon_Chisel@BlindMud` for a palette variant and `AE_Rope@NECROPE` for a file one), with its hold count, loop flag, loop start and per frame the sheet, the rectangle and the engine's own frame offsets. The sheets sit under `cams/` so the worker's cache-first rule stores them beside the cameras, but outside the cache stamp: a game's sheets are one set in a directory named for their pixels and shape (`sheet_set_name`), which the sidecar's `sheets` carries, so a changed sheet reaches visitors under a new URL and leaves every stored camera in place. The build writes the set and then removes the game's others, so the directory only ever holds the set the sidecar names; and a set named for pixels rather than bytes keeps its name through `--reencode-images`. The sidecar is fetched at boot when the view opens with the objects shown, else the first time the toggle turns on. The set also holds `font.png`, the LCD screens' font as an **index map** rather than texels: `LCDFONT.FNT`'s 4bpp texture with each texel's palette index in every channel, opaque throughout, since a screen colours its glyphs through palettes compiled into its own code and swaps them at every message end; the sidecar's `font` names that sheet, its size and the glyph table read off the executable, which the file does not hold ([docs/format-gotchas.md](format-gotchas.md) has the shape the table is found by).
  - `tools/data/sprite_anims.json` is **hand-curated**, like `annotations.json`: it names each animation's file, resource id and ordinal in the chunk's table per game. The names are the relive beta's `AnimId` enumerators (`Zap_Sparks` the pinned master's, the beta filing that chunk as `ChantOrb_Particle_Small`) and the ordinals were solved from its PC byte offsets against the PS1 tables (the table region's layout is the same sequence of header sizes on both platforms, so several records in one chunk pin the alignment), then checked by eye; a name the discs cannot answer fails the build rather than shipping a hole.
  - A rebuild re-packs and re-encodes the whole sheet, every version of which history keeps, and every visitor storing artwork downloads it again; so animations are gathered into as few rebuilds as possible, and a sheet may carry an animation before the rule or brain that draws it. `SHIPPED_AHEAD` in `tests/unit/sprites.test.js` names each such animation per game: the test fails a shipped animation that nothing draws and nothing lists, and a listed one that something draws, so an animation leaves the list in the commit that draws it.
  - The frames pack by a shelf packer over sorted keys and identical frames pack once, so the sheets are byte-deterministic through `write_png` like the cameras; a frame's alpha is 0, 254 or 255 (clear, the semi-transparency bit, opaque), and `--reencode-images` re-emits the sheets with the rest of the artwork. Each animation also carries its first frame's bounding rectangle, which the platforms stand by, and the Exoddus sidecar the path table's Abe starts, which the game places a few devices against. The sidecar also carries each path's collision-line links (`links`, the `previous` and `next` indices the engine's line following hops by, the same columns `tools/data/lines_*` holds) and the engine's random table, the one 256-byte run of the disc's executable holding every byte value once, which is how `read_dice` finds it without an address; it is read from every disc the build touched and the copies must agree.
- `levels/**` and `sitemap.xml`: generated **and committed** search-engine surface — one plain HTML page per level plus the `/levels/` index, each deep-linking into the viewer, and the sitemap naming them all. Emitted by `node tools/levelpages.js` (no disc) from `map_data_{ao,ae}.json` + `annotations.json`, reusing the viewer's own bare-Node modules for names, play order and demo exclusion; never hand-edit.
  - Deterministic over its inputs, and `tests/unit/levelpages.test.js` byte-compares the committed files against a fresh emit — so a rebuild or an `annotations.json` edit needs a re-emit in the same commit, and CI fails until it happens.
  - A page's screen is its entry path's first stored camera, unless the emitter's `SCREEN_OVERRIDES` table pins another as the level's face; a pin naming a level or screen the data doesn't hold, a pin on the default pick, or a page screen without artwork all fail the emit rather than standing stale.
  - The pages are content, not redirects: a crawler indexes a redirect's destination with the `#` fragment dropped, so a redirecting stub would collapse into the homepage.
  - They live nested under `levels/` on purpose — an HTML page reaches the worker's shell rule only at the site root, and nothing else that rule matches (the `js/`/`css/` trees, the named icons) lives here — so no level page can enter or displace the shell cache, and the pages stay out of the offline story entirely.
- Static site files that are not the viewer or its data (all in `public/`): `favicon.svg` (source of truth for the icon; `favicon-96.png` and `apple-touch-icon.png` are rasterized from it), `og-image.png` (1200×630 social card, rendered by `tools/ogcard.swift` — edit the script and rerun it, don't touch the PNG directly), `404.html` (the not-found page — self-contained, every URL on it root-absolute, since Pages serves it at whatever missing address was asked), `site.webmanifest`, `robots.txt`, `CNAME` (oddworldmap.com).
  - Regenerate the icon PNGs from the SVG if the icon changes (a CoreGraphics Swift script was used; any SVG rasterizer works).

## `python3 tools/build_map.py`

- `cam2rgba` is compiled automatically on first run; `oxipng` must be installed at exactly `OXIPNG_VERSION` ([tools/oddmap/image.py](../tools/oddmap/image.py)), which `ensure_oxipng` checks before a strip is decoded. Every emitted PNG is losslessly recompressed with `-o 2 --strip safe --force`, and the bytes are oxipng's alone — the builder hands it plain RGBA8 and it chooses the colour type, the palette and the filters, the `--force` keeping a file it cannot shrink from staying the raw write, whose deflate stream is CPython's zlib's — so they move between its releases: 10.2.0's indexed-image work re-encoded 364 of the 1130 masks the 10.1.1 tree held, pixel-identical, and left every RGB cam alone. A bump is the Prettier rule — move the constant and `--reencode-images` the tree in a commit of its own — and `test_build_map.py` re-emits the committed masks and a sample of the cams at the pin wherever an oxipng is on PATH (never in CI, which has none), so a tree and a pin that disagree fail the suite on the machine that would build; an oxipng off the pin fails it outright rather than skipping, refused as the builder would refuse it.
- The pipeline is byte-deterministic. To verify builder changes, build into a scratch dir with `--out` and `cmp` the data file (and spot-check PNGs) against the committed outputs.
- `--levels X,Y` subset builds merge into the existing data file — they do not clobber other levels.
- Existing cam PNGs are skipped for speed, so a level whose decode previously half-completed keeps stale outputs; delete `public/cams/<game>/<LEVEL>/` for a clean rebuild of that level.
- `python3 tools/build_map.py --reencode-images` re-emits every PNG under `--out/cams` from its own pixels through `write_png` at the pinned oxipng and restamps `CACHE_NAME`, no disc needed: the committed pixels are the builder's own raw input, and `read_png` reads them back from whatever colour type oxipng reduced them to. It is the encoding half of a rebuild, so it is what re-encodes the tree when the oxipng it encodes with moves, and a scratch `--out` holding no worker stamps nothing, like a build.
